audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer is built on an ability called 'Twofold Hunt' (sometimes 'Twofold Hunt (Blink)'). No such ability exists, and the two halves of the invented name belong to different spells.
audit.why: Aurora's kit is Spirit Abjuration (P), Twofold Hex (Q, 9s at 900 range), Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18 at 700), The Weirding (E, 15s at 825) and Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100). The blink the text describes as 'her escape' is Across the Veil — which is also the W, so focus.letters was already right.
audit.corrected: Every 'Twofold Hunt' reassigned to Across the Veil; focus.text set to 'Across the Veil (W)'.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is never stated: Across the Veil makes Aurora invisible on landing, and Shield Vault is a targeted dash.
audit.why: Riot's Across the Veil text: she 'leaps in a direction of her choosing, entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible'. Riot's Shield Vault text: 'Pantheon dashes to a target'. A target he cannot see is a target he cannot select — so her W does not merely dodge the stun, it removes your ability to cast it for 22 seconds at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil breaks Shield Vault's target lock; play the lane on its 22s.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1], wants.you[1] and early all tell you to play around 'her root'. Aurora has no root.
audit.why: The Weirding damages and slows, then hops her backward; Between Worlds damages and slows and leaves a slowing zone. Riot's text has no root anywhere in the kit. Waiting out a root that does not exist means eating the real threat, which is Twofold Hex's recast dragging the curse back through you.
audit.corrected: Root references replaced with Twofold Hex's recast and The Weirding's slow-plus-hop-back.

audit.why: TRICKY 7.5/10 fits 52.89% over 762 games with a chart that gives Aurora level 1 and level 6. Early lane is a range problem — Twofold Hex reaches 900, Comet Spear 575 — and the side lane belongs to her AP scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere and no real ability names in the spike rows.
audit.why: Across the Veil 22s at rank 1, Twofold Hex 9s, The Weirding 15s, Between Worlds 140s. Against Shield Vault's 13s, the Veil being twice your gap-closer's cooldown is the whole reason you get windows at all.
audit.corrected: Spikes and cooldown block now carry the names and numbers.

audit.why: Mercury's Treads and Doran's Shield are right into a 900-range magic poke lane. Spirit Abjuration heals her off every spell she lands, so Grievous Wounds has value in extended fights, though her lane pressure is burst rather than sustain.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are mine. At level 1 my W stun is point-and-click and she has no E blink yet to dodge it, so I can W in, tapped-Q reset, and chunk her before she ever pokes. Bait her Q out, then hold my E directional block to eat her root and follow-up rather than committing into it. Force the trade every time her blink is down — she has no answer to a level-2 or level-3 all-in before her mobility comes online.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are mine. At level 1 Shield Vault dashes 600 onto her with a stun and she has no Across the Veil yet, so I W in, tapped-Q reset, and chunk her before she pokes. Bait Twofold Hex out and face her so Aegis Assault eats the recast dragging the curse back. Force the trade every time the Veil is down — she has no answer to a level-2 or level-3 all-in before it comes online.

edits.before: Through 4-5 I still control her with empowered-Q poke and E blocks, but raw kill pressure dips as she stabilizes and gets her blink reliably up — pick my W timings when her E is on cooldown, not on instinct. At 6 the lane tilts: her ult and W exile plus the E blink let her sidestep my W gap-close and kite my low-HP frame, so my own R is better spent roaming to bot or mid than chasing a 1v1 I no longer cleanly win.
edits.after: Through 4-5 I still control her with empowered-Q poke and Aegis Assault, but kill pressure dips once Across the Veil is reliably up — its 22s against my 13s Shield Vault is the whole window, so I pick W timings off her Veil, not on instinct. At 6 the lane tilts: landing in the spirit realm she goes invisible and my targeted W has nothing to click, so Grand Starfall is better spent roaming than chasing.

notes: _missing-interactions.json claims 'Aurora can cancel your Aegis Assault (E) with Between Worlds (R)'. Riot's Between Worlds text describes damage, a slow and a traversable zone — no stun, no knockup, nothing that interrupts a channel. The kit's hardCC flag looks like a tooltip-parse misfire, so I did not write that interaction; logged in unverified. Aurora also has no root anywhere in her kit, yet three strings told you to play around one — corrected. Spirit Abjuration does heal her off every spell she lands, which supports the existing Grievous Wounds line, but her lane threat is burst rather than sustain so I did not promote anti-heal into the core build.
